content.en: The **Human Poverty Index (HPI)** was introduced to capture the **multidimensional** nature of poverty. Unlike income-based poverty lines, HPI focuses on the **deprivation** of essential capabilities. It evaluates the quality of life by assessing three key dimensions: **longevity** (probability of not surviving to a certain age), **knowledge** (adult illiteracy rates), and a **decent standard of living** (access to clean water, health services, and child nutrition).

content.en: HPI-1 was designed for developing countries, while HPI-2 was tailored for selected high-income OECD countries to reflect social exclusion.

content.en: Do not confuse HPI with the Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI); MPI replaced HPI in later reports.
